# mvdan.cc/sh fork

This directory is a fork of [`mvdan.cc/sh/v3`](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) at `v3.14.1`, kept under its upstream BSD-3-Clause license (`LICENSE`), as ADR-0030 in z-shell/.github decides. `go.mod` at the repository root replaces the module with this directory, so import paths are unchanged.

Only the packages zsh-lint builds are kept: `syntax`, `expand`, `pattern`, `fileutil`, and `internal`. Upstream's tests for them are kept and run in Go CI; they must keep passing.

## Local changes

Every change is Zsh-only, behind `LangZsh`, and listed here with the zsh-lint issue that made it.

| Change | Files | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rejection of a lone `-` condition (`condition expected: -`), and rejection of `!` or leading `(` in the right operand of `<` and `>`, matching native Zsh condlex and par_cond_2 | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/module_test.go` | [#512](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/512) |
| Module-defined prefix and infix conditions, multi-operand dash conditions, and lone unary-name string tests, with a Zsh-only `ModuleTest` node, positions, walk, printer and typedjson support; in their operands a glob group nests bare parentheses and numeric globs, and `;`, `&` or a bare `<`/`>` inside the group is an error, as Zsh's word lexer reads it | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/nodes.go`, `syntax/walk.go`, `syntax/printer.go`, `syntax/typedjson/`, `syntax/module_test.go` | [#484](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/484) |
| Brace-form `if`/`elif`/`else` and `while`/`until` bodies (Alternate Forms For Complex Commands) | `syntax/parser.go` | [#446](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/446) |
| A `'` in the word of a double-quoted `${...}` is text, not a single-quote opener | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go` | [#400](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/400) |
| In a glob group or glob qualifier, a quoted `)` and the `)` closing a command substitution do not end the group | `syntax/parser.go` | [#439](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/439) |
| A case pattern whose leading group is glued to more pattern text, `(x)y)`, and a leading `((`, as in `((x\|y)\|z)` | `syntax/parser.go` | [#452](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/452) |
| In a case item that begins with `(`, a `#` glued to the opener, to a `\|` in that group, or to the `)` closing a leading group is pattern text, not a comment, as in the globbing flag `(#i)x)` and `(x)#)` | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go` | [#482](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/482) |
| In a case item that begins with `(`, a blank inside a bracket expression of the opener's group is pattern text, as in `(a[ b]*)` and `(a[$x b])`; the printer writes the opening `(` for a pattern holding such a blank. | A `((` that continues a word opens a glob group whose first byte opens a nested group, as in `x((b)c)` in a case pattern, an argument, an assignment value or a redirect target, rather than an arithmetic command; a `((` that starts a word keeps upstream's reading | `syntax/parser.go` | [#481](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/481) |
| A case pattern with an empty alternative, such as `(\|a)`, `(a\|)`, `\|a)`, `a\|)`, `\|a\|)`, `(a\|\|b)`, `(\|)`, `\|\|)`, and `(\|a\|)` | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#396](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/396) |
| The alternate and short forms of `for` and `select` (several names, a `( word ... )` list, a `{ list }` or one-sublist body, an empty body), the short forms of `if`, `while` and `until`, `else` reserved in command position, and a `ZshEnd` position on `ForClause`, `IfClause` and `WhileClause` so `End()` is exact for those forms | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/nodes.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#459](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/459) |
| The csh-style `foreach ... end` loop (one or more names, `( word ... )` or `in word ...`, `list end`, `{ list }` or `do list done`), and `end` reserved in command position | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/nodes.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#214](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/214) |

| Function definitions whose name is any word, holding a parameter expansion, quote or command substitution (`word()` and `function word ...`), and a name ending in a `}` that closes no `{` of the name rejected as zsh does | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#234](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/234) |
| Semicolons and newlines between the case word and `in` (`case word; in`) | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#485](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/485) |
| After an assignment prefix, `!`, `[[`, `{`, `(`, `time`, `coproc`, `if`, `case`, `while`, `until`, `for`, `select`, `foreach` and `function` are rejected, and a closing reserved word (`then`, `fi`, `do`, `done`, `esac`, `end`, ...) ends the command, as Zsh keeps command position after the prefix | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#278](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/278) |
| A `function` keyword definition whose body is missing or is itself a bodyless or keyword definition defines each name with an empty body (`FuncDecl.Body == nil`), with `ParensEnd` for `End()`, printer, and walk support | `syntax/nodes.go`, `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/printer.go`, `syntax/walk.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#479](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/479) |
| A subscripted or array assignment before a command word (`a[2]=x cmd`, `a=(x y) cmd`) is an ordinary prefix assignment; upstream's `inline variables cannot be arrays` error stays for Bash | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#285](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/285) |
| A braced `${+` must be followed by a parameter name; a nested expansion, quote, special parameter or operator after it is an error, as in Zsh | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#363](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/363) |
| A glob group in any word ends the word at `;`, `&`, or a `<` or `>` that starts neither a process substitution nor a numeric glob `<m-n>`, as Zsh's lexer does; a `(` inside a parameter expansion in the group opens nothing; a `)` left over by such a word in `[[ ]]` is reported where it stands | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/glob_group_word_test.go`, `syntax/module_test.go` | [#511](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/511) |
| Outside double quotes, braces nest in the word of a `${...}`, so `${x:-{}}` is one expansion and `${x:-{}` is unclosed; a nested expansion keeps its own count; a nested expansion, and a here-document body, count as double-quoted for the #400 quote rule | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go`, `syntax/param_word_brace_test.go` | [#518](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/518) |
| An `=~` operand ends inside a group at `;`, `&`, or a `<` or `>` that starts neither a process substitution nor a numeric glob `<m-n>`, as any other Zsh word does; a `)` left over after `&&` names the outermost open `(` | `syntax/lexer.go`, `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/regex_group_word_test.go` | [#517](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/517) |
| A `(` directly followed by `)` ends a word inside a glob group, a condition operand's group, or an `=~` operand, as `()` is a token of its own in Zsh; an empty process substitution `<()` is not such a `(` | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go`, `syntax/empty_group_test.go`, `syntax/parser_test.go` | [#522](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/522) |
| In an unquoted `${...}`, a `{` in the subscript counts toward the expansion's braces, as Zsh's lexer counts them: a balanced `{...}` is text, blanks, operators and a flag argument's `,` included, and a `{` still open at the `]` is an error. Zsh also accepts such a `{` when text after the expansion closes it, as in `x=${x[{]}}`, which the parser has no place for and rejects: a known false rejection | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go`, `syntax/subscript_brace_test.go` | [#521](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/521) |
| The body of a command substitution, backquoted command or process substitution that a glob group reader keeps as text is parsed on its own, and an error in it is reported at its place in the source; backquote escapes are removed first, and a `$((` body that may be arithmetic is left as before | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/group_subst_body_test.go` | [#519](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/519) |
| The raw subscript-flag argument reader follows a command substitution or backquoted command in the argument and parses its body when it closes, as the glob group reader does; a `,` inside it is text, a `'` is not quoting (the subscript reads as double-quoted), and `<(` is a pattern, not a process substitution | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/flag_subst_body_test.go` | [#526](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/526) |
| In a raw subscript-flag argument, a `]` inside a `$(...)`, `$((...))` or (in a `${...}`) backquoted body is text of the body; in a `${...}` the `[` and `]` of those bodies must balance over the subscript, and a `]` in a backquoted body must close an earlier `[` | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/flag_subst_bracket_test.go` | [#529](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/529) |
| In a command or array word, a bare `(` inside a glob group nests, so only its matching `)` closes it, as in `f=( (a|(b|c)) )`; `[[ ]]` operands keep their nested groups to the conditional-pattern adapter. A nested group left open to the end of input is rejected, although `zsh -f -n` accepts it: a known false rejection for assignments such as `x=a(b(c)`, the class `x=a(b` already had | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/nested_glob_group_word_test.go` | [#397](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/397) |
| In a raw subscript-flag argument, a short subscript with flags, as in `$y[(r)a]`, is text of the argument, so its `]` no longer ends the argument; a `[` left open in the argument's own text is still not counted, a known false accept filed as #534 | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/flag_short_subscript_test.go` | [#532](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/532) |
| The `[` and `]` bytes inside the command substitutions of a `${...}` subscript must balance over the whole subscript, across a `,` and in an unflagged subscript; the lexer records the subscript's bytes while it is read and the check runs once it is parsed | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/lexer.go`, `syntax/subscript_bracket_balance_test.go` | [#531](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/531) |
| In a `${...}` subscript flag argument, a `[` of the argument's own text, quoted or not, that is still open where the reader stops at the subscript's `]` is reported; brackets inside a nested `${...}` are its own, and a `[` open at a `,` is left as before | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/flag_open_bracket_test.go` | [#534](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/534) |
| In a short `$x[...]` subscript flag argument, a `[` of the argument's own text still open at the `]` the reader stops at is reported when no later `]` of the same lexical word closes it; the read-ahead follows quotes, glob groups, numeric globs and nested expansions, whose brackets are their own | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/short_flag_open_bracket_test.go` | [#538](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/538) |
| The `IfClause` of a brace-form `else` leaves `ThenPos` empty, as a classic `else` does, instead of holding the body's `{`; the printer and `IfClause` readers treat a clause with a `ThenPos` as an `elif` | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/zsh_brace_else_test.go` | [#541](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/541) |
| The printer writes `()` after the names of a `function` keyword definition whose body is not a `{ }` group, since Zsh reads every word before a `{` as another name | `syntax/printer.go`, `syntax/zsh_print_func_test.go` | [#541](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/541) |
| The printer writes a case item's optional opening parenthesis when an alternative ends in an unquoted literal `}`, which Zsh would otherwise read as closing a brace group | `syntax/printer.go`, `syntax/zsh_print_case_test.go` | [#541](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/541) |
| The #538 read-ahead finds the short subscript's word end by shell quoting, then counts `[`, `]`, `(` and `)` over that text with `dquote_parse` rules: `'` is text outside backquotes, `"` outside a nested `${...}`, a `$(...)` body is skipped and a nested `${...}` does not count brackets; a backquote the subscript's text leaves open when read as a string, as in ``$x[(r)a[b]'`'`echo "]"` ``, is reported at that backquote | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/short_flag_dquote_rules_test.go` | [#540](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/540) |
| A `&&` or `\|\|` takes the first statement after any `;` and newline separators as its right operand, as Zsh's `par_sublist` skips them, so `a && ; b` is the sublist `a && b`; when only the end of the list follows the separators, the error stays at the operator for the dangling-operator adapter | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/zsh_andor_separator_test.go` | [#548](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/548) |
| A `\|` or `\|&` takes the first command after any `;` and newline separators as its right operand, as Zsh's `par_pline` skips them, so `a \| ; b` is the pipeline `a \| b`; when only the end of the list follows the separators, the error stays at the operator, since Zsh never lets a pipe dangle | `syntax/parser.go`, `syntax/zsh_pipe_separator_test.go` | [#553](https://github.com/z-shell/zsh-lint/issues/553) |

## Taking an upstream release

Copy the new release's packages over this directory, reapply the changes above, and run upstream's tests here and zsh-lint's full suite, with the tree-shape checks ADR-0023 point 3 requires.
